newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung sets up teams to tackle post-97 problems.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung sets up teams to tackle post-97 problems.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Friday appointed three officials to launch action programmes to solve key bread-and-butter problems in the territory after Britain hands it back to China this year.

"I'm inviting three executive councillors with special knowledge and ability to help me in mapping out long-term strategies in the areas of housing, education and policies for the elderly," he told reporters at a news conference.

The three -- Leung Chun-ying responsible for housing, Antony Leung for education and Tam Yiu-chung for elderly services -- will work closely with principal officials and senior civil servants in mapping out their strategies, Tung said.
"The three members and government officials will put forward their views in helping me to devise these policies ... in looking for constructive and innovative changes," he said.
But Tung's plan has met with opposition from some of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people, who will be under Chinese rule from midnight on June 30 when Britain pulls out.
Early morning radio programmes were jammed on Friday by calls from the public slamming Tung's choice of property surveyor Leung Chun-ying as they feared a conflict of interest.
But Tung dismissed such suggestions from reporters, saying he was confident of Leung's ability and integrity.
